messages:
anjali: FYI getting a customer escalation — ACME reports sudden p99 spikes from EU users to our text-gen endpoint starting ~09:12 UTC. They say requests are routing via APAC proxies. attaching their trace snippet below.

alan: can you paste the trace + trace id? also which model/route are they hitting?

anjali: trace id 01F8XQ3Z, route /v1/generate, model xlarge-2. They gave this traceroute: 

```
> traceroute to api.redwood.example.com (13.224.45.67), 30 hops max
1  10.0.0.1 (10.0.0.1)  0.7 ms
2  edge-eu-01.redwood.internal (10.12.1.5)  1.9 ms
3  transit-eu-01 (52.28.1.1)  4.5 ms
4  sg-proxy-1.ap.redwood.example.com (103.12.11.7)  120.3 ms
5  api.redwood.example.com (13.224.45.67)  121.0 ms
```

anjali: customer says historically hops 3->5 were under 15ms and never went via sg-proxy-1.

cheng: weird. any recent LB config changes? infra-bot, did any routing policy flips or fallback rules trigger?

infra-bot: deploy-log: routing-policy/weighted-fallback v2 deployed by @ops-ci at 2026-03-17T08:55:12Z. A/B rollout to 5% of eu-origin traffic.

alan: that deployment could explain a small percent of traffic hitting APAC fallback. but 100% of ACME requests? are they on a dedicated plan or hosted?

anjali: hosted, but high volume — they hit rate limits until yesterday then increased throughput. they claim all their EU requests are affected this morning (seen in their graph).

julie: I pulled our edge logs for trace 01F8XQ3Z — I see origin ASN mapping says client ip -> eu-region but LB decision shows `fallback=edge:ap-northeast-1` and the request got tagged `route_reason=fallback:capacity`. snippet: 

```
2026-03-17T09:12:03Z INFO request_id=01F8XQ3Z origin_region=eu-west-1 lb_decision=fallback target_edge=sg-proxy-1 reason=shortage:dedicated_gpus
```

julie: so seems capacity fallback triggered, choosing APAC proxy due to dedicated GPU shortages in eu cluster.

sre_oncall: can we repro? alan, can you run a synthetic from eu and capture full trace + tcpdump? we should also check the capacity alarms around 09:10-09:20.

alan: running a quick curl from our eu-prober: `curl -v -H "X-Request-ID: repro-240123" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate` — getting 120ms RTT and server header `edge:sg-proxy-1`. attaching minimal tcpdump: 

```
09:18:12.123 IP eu-prober > sg-proxy-1: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
09:18:12.245 IP sg-proxy-1 > eu-prober: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1, win 65535
```

alan: confirms eu probe routed to sg-proxy-1.

cheng: action items: 1) verify why fallback triggered for dedicated customers (policy mis-eval?), 2) check rollout percentage and immediately rollback weighted-fallback if it's hitting production volume beyond canary, 3) mitigate for ACME now (route pinning).

anjali: paging product for emergency pin for ACME key — can we create a temporary tenant-pin for eu region until capacity restored?

julie: filed a support escalation with ACME and requested request IDs for all affected samples. adding note to case: `mitigate by tenant-pin eu-region` and `rollback routing-policy/weighted-fallback v2`.

infra-bot: alert: dedicated-gpu-eu usage at 102% of soft-cap at 2026-03-17T08:58:03Z. Autoscale attempted +1 but failed due to quota.

alan: quota failure explains shortage. ops to engage cloud quota team; in parallel I'll rollback the routing policy to v1.

cheng: SGTM. also add a check in the policy evaluator to avoid fallback for tenants above `reserved_tier=true`. that would have prevented hosteds with reserved capacity from being bumped.

anjali: thanks team. I'll update ACME with repro steps (trace id + traceroute) and ETA for mitigation. will post updates here. :thumbsup:
